data.title: The Chalk
data.text:
You went through No. 14 Church Lane and the Pells' house next door, then the Riverside dam gave way. Eight houses went. I had marked No. 14 with a circle crossed by a line: empty. Inside were the calendar, a piano nobody had tuned in years, and the archive boxes. I was still holding the chalk. The wardens had tested it in rain. It did not help against water.

Gil Harrow wrote that the spillway had been deferred because the national inspectors called the dam satisfactory, the harbour needed dredging, the school roof leaked, and he believed there was time. At the levy vote, No had more votes than Yes. The wall came later, built to the old design. I kept the chalk.
